result.title: GeoVLDrive: Geometry-Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) planners inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained vision-language models, but their reasoning is rarely grounded in 3D scene structure and its evolution over time. We introduce GeoVLDrive, a geometry-grounded VLA framework for 3D spatiotemporal reasoning and planning. Multi-layer features from a 3D foundation model augment the vision-language backbone through gated cross-attention. A structured latent chain of thought (CoT) organizes future scene geometry, key-agent motion, and meta-actions into ordered, separately supervised latent states. An action expert generates trajectory proposals from these states and multi-layer scene features, and ranks them using scene-grounded, interacting score tokens. We also introduce NAVSIM 3DQA to train and evaluate metric 3D spatial and motion understanding. GeoVLDrive achieves 91.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2. On NAVSIM 3DQA, the geometry-grounded backbone scores 89.2% overall, 4.6 percentage points above the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B baseline. On LingoQA, the backbone achieves 68.6% Lingo-Judge accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: GeoVLDrive 提出一种几何接地的驾驶 VLA 框架，用 3D 基础模型多层特征增强视觉语言主干，并将未来场景几何、关键智能体运动与元动作组织为有序、分别监督的 latent CoT 状态，再由动作专家生成并排序轨迹。
AI.relevance_reason: 其结构化 latent 状态及分项监督直接关联 LVR 中推理状态表示、视觉证据注入与贡献分配问题，但研究场景为自动驾驶规划，需核查 latent 状态是否真正承载并驱动最终决策。
